"The positivity to natural affection displayed by this father for his son has none of the Lutheran total depravity doctrine, and it accords with the Catholic analogia entis pattern. Now in the natural love of this father for his son behold the goodness of God, who is far more clement to sinful man, if only he repents and despises himself, than any father to his son, however tenderly he may love him."

This passage is from the Method of True Theology, which was originally the Preface to the first edition of his New Testament, but it is used in a broader context discussing mystical, pastoral and personal/political moral concerns instead.

Regarding Theological Writings, we may distinguish four different lines of work, parallel with each other, and complementary. First, the establishing and critical elucidation of the biblical texts; alongside it, the editions of the great patristic commentators; then, the exegetical works properly so called, in which these two fundamental researches yield their fruit; and finally, the methodological works, which in their first state constitute a sort of preface to the various other studies, but which—in return—were nourished by these other studies as well."
